teams.body: Fiji's next assignment is the trip to France on the calendar. The log has them winless from three outings, with 49 points scored and 145 conceded for a difference of -96. Against that backdrop, the trip to France is a real test of where the side stands. Their most recent result was a 34-28 win over Japan.

teams.heading: Bill Sweeney says England must cut yellow cards after Six Nations sin-binnings
teams.body: Discipline is on the agenda before Sunday's meeting with Australia, the opener of England's November campaign. England picked up eight yellow cards and one red across their five Six Nations matches, playing 118 minutes at less than a full complement. Sweeney says analysis suggests England drop to eighth or ninth best in the world when down to 14 players, and that Steve Borthwick is working with the squad on it. "It has been a big internal discussion," Sweeney said.

lead.why: RFU chief Bill Sweeney's public call on England's discipline is a fresh, on-record England story with hard figures and a direct quote, ahead of the Australia match.

teams.heading: Galthié names Regis Montagne among five new faces in 42-man France squad
teams.body: Fabien Galthié has added five players to France's Nations Championship squad, taking the group to 42. Clermont prop Regis Montagne is in as cover for Bayonne's Tevita Tatafu, while Montpellier lock Florian Verhaeghe, Toulouse prop Rodrigue Neti and uncapped Clermont centre Leon Darricarrere complete the changes. The additions come ahead of the Springboks' visit to the Stade de France and the Argentina test that follows.

teams.heading: Ulster re-sign Jacob Stockdale, Nick Timoney and Tom O'Toole until 2030
teams.body: Ulster have tied down five senior players, including four Ireland internationals, on contracts running until at least 2030. James Hume, Tom O'Toole, Jacob Stockdale and Nick Timoney have all won Test caps, and Ethan McIlroy has been drafted into Ireland's November squad. General manager Rory Best said Ulster were "very pleased to have secured the futures" of the five, who have a combined 650 appearances between them and all came through the club's youth ranks.

teams.heading: Italy mark ten years since Florence win over Springboks with Turin tribute
teams.body: The FIR has laid on a pre-match tribute to the 19 November 2016 win at Florence's Artemio Franchi, Italy's first historic triumph over the Springboks. Former Azzurri from that day will receive awards from federation president, after a speech from some players who featured ten years ago. Proceeds from a charity auction of Nicola Russo's TOH artwork and shirts signed by both squads go to the INOC Candiolo cancer institute, and ticket holders can book a free male cancer check.

lead.why: It is a fresh, Italy-specific event on matchday that gives the reader something new to point to beyond the injury and scrum coverage already run this week.

teams.heading: Tom English expects competitive All Blacks defeat, then wins over Australia and Japan
teams.body: BBC Sport's Tom English expects Scotland to lose a competitive contest with New Zealand on Saturday, then beat Australia and Japan, though he would not rule out three wins from three. He points to the recent record: Scotland trailed 17-0 the last time they met the All Blacks and were 14-0 down the time before. His warning is that Dave Rennie's side are at their wiliest when the heat comes on, and Scotland start to make mistakes at the breakdown and lineout.

lead.why: The freshest NEW item with concrete context, and it sets out Scotland's realistic autumn expectations ahead of Saturday's All Blacks test.

teams.heading: Tandy set to pair Llewellyn and James in midfield against Japan
teams.body: WalesOnline understands Tandy will drop the dual-playmaker approach favoured by attack coach Matt Sherratt, with Sam Costelow at fly-half and Max Llewellyn and Eddie James expected to form the midfield partnership. Llewellyn has started at inside centre only once for Wales, against England in a 2023 warm-up, while Tandy has said that James is "more of a 13 who can play 12" in the Wales set-up. Louie Hennessey is set to be named among the replacements.

teams.heading: Contepomi says a Dublin win would be a bonus, with performance first
teams.body: Felipe Contepomi puts performance ahead of the result for Friday's test, saying Argentina's first task is to be competitive. Argentina have never beaten Ireland away from home in 11 meetings, and the coach said ending that run is not the chief motivator. "It would mean a lot, but I think more so it is for us to try to get better," he said. Contepomi said the 28-24 win over the Lions at the Aviva in June 2025 offers little, since every game starts from zero.

teams.heading: Angus Bell says Wallabies have fixed Bledisloe problems ahead of England Test
teams.body: Prop Angus Bell says the Wallabies have fixed what went wrong against the All Blacks, whose quick ball and fast breakdown exposed their movement speed in two heavy defeats that ended a six-game unbeaten run. Bell says the changes have been implemented at training. Australia sit third in the South on nine points, behind New Zealand and South Africa, the only undefeated sides on 15. Asked what success looks like, Bell answered "Three from three," with Scotland and Wales still to come after England.

teams.heading: Tyrel Lomax dropped from tour squad; Jason Ryan backs scrum improvement
teams.body: All Blacks coach Dave Rennie has cited the injury Lomax played through against South Africa, and the tighthead missed both Bledisloe Cup Tests. Scrum coach Jason Ryan says the set-piece began turning the tide late in the Springboks series and carried that into the Wallaby Tests; Scott Barrett has added power on the tighthead side. Uncapped prop Saula Ma'u gets his chance, while Ethan De Groot returns to fitness and will compete with George Bower for the loosehead jersey.

teams.heading: Italy's Ferrari expects Springboks to kick high and test Azzurri backs
teams.body: Ferrari, speaking to the Italian federation this week, expects South Africa to kick high and challenge Italy's backs in the air, and says the Springboks rarely concede chances, so Italy must take every one they create. He also expects a hard-fought scrum battle, with Italy knowing the Springboks' props well. With many Italian players unavailable, Ferrari says squad depth has kept quality intact.

lead.why: The freshest item not already run this week, and it sets out how Italy expect the Springboks to play.
